note: Direction selectors and resume choices for role_library.py (JSA-249). selector picks the JDs (jobs.track, optional title / text regex); section_order, headline_pattern and angles are the resume choices for that direction (angles = how a bullet proving that competency should be told). The statistics (weights, keywords) are generated into roles/<direction>.json. template = harvard (education first, Leadership & Activities) or jakes (projects / experience first, compact skills block) — both rendered by build_a.py (JSA-253).

ai_pm.label: AI Product Manager / AI Product Analytics

or_tracks_with_text.regex: \b(LLMs?|large language models?|generative AI|GenAI|AI[- ]powered|machine learning|AI agents?|agentic|AI products?)\b

ai_pm.headline_pattern: <exact job title> · <2–4 true JD terms: AI / product / evaluation first>

angles.ai_eval: what was evaluated, the criteria or rubric, the human check, and the decision or time it changed
angles.llm_genai: the LLM in a real workflow: what it did, what stayed with a person, the measurable effect
angles.agents: the system's job for its user, how work is split across agents, and the guardrail that keeps it truthful
angles.product_sense: the user problem first, then the decision he made (scope, priority, rule) and its outcome
angles.metrics: the metric chosen, why it matters for the decision, and the result
angles.stakeholders: who used the output and how it changed their work
angles.experimentation: the question, the test design that keeps it honest, and what the result did or did not show
angles.ownership: what he owned end to end and what shipped

data_analyst.label: Data Analyst / BI
data_analyst.headline_pattern: <exact job title> · SQL · <BI tool or Python / R from the JD>

angles.sql: the data joined or queried and the question it answered
angles.bi_viz: the dashboard or chart, who used it, the decision it supported
angles.data_quality: the mismatch found, how it was fixed, what became comparable
angles.metrics: the metric, the comparison, the business result
angles.statistics: the method and what it showed, with the honest caveat
angles.stakeholders: the audience and the faster or better decision
angles.excel: the model built and who relied on it

data_engineer.label: Data Engineer
data_engineer.headline_pattern: <exact job title> · Python · SQL · <pipeline / cloud tool from the JD>

angles.pipelines: sources in, rows out, what the pipeline guarantees
angles.data_quality: the rule (normalization, dedup, validation) and the before / after counts
angles.cloud_data: the platform and what was built on it
angles.data_modeling: the model or schema and who queries it
angles.automation: what runs without a person and how failures are caught
angles.sql: the query work and its scale

ai_agentic.label: AI / Agentic Engineer
ai_agentic.headline_pattern: <exact job title> · LLM agents · <2–3 true JD terms>

angles.agents: the agents, the orchestration, and what each one is trusted to do
angles.llm_genai: the model in the loop and how its output is checked
angles.ai_eval: the evaluation or guardrail and what it catches
angles.automation: the end-to-end flow and the human approval point
angles.python: what the code does, at what scale
angles.software_eng: the interfaces and tests that keep it reliable
